newsitem.title: USA: FAA ValuJet inspector not qualified-report.
newsitem.headline: FAA ValuJet inspector not qualified-report.

text.p: A Federal Aviation Administration official in charge of ValuJet maintenance at the time of a crash that killed 110 people was not qualified for the position, the Cleveland Plain Dealer reported Sunday.
FAA officials declined to comment on the report on Monday.
"The FAA can not comment on ongoing investigations on the part of the inspector general," FAA spokesman Fraser Jones said.

The newspaper said a 122-page report by the Transportation Department's Office of Inspector General reported that FAA inspector David J. Harper did not have enough civilian aviation experience to properly oversee ValuJet maintenance and falsified his experience.
Harper oversaw ValuJet maintenance from September 1994 to August last year, the newspaper reported.

On May 11, 1996, 110 people were killed when ValuJet's Flight 592 crashed in the Florida Everglades after a fire erupted on the Atlanta-bound DC-9 shortly after taking off from Miami International Airport.
